notes: Full document chain present: purchase order (PO-1014), invoice (INV-1014) referencing the PO and vendor's own numbering, a goods receipt note (REC-1014) confirming physical delivery, a ledger entry (LED-1014), and a bank statement (BNK-1014) recording payment. All documents cross-reference each other consistently and amounts align (invoice total INR 246,000 = INR 200,000 subtotal + INR 36,000 GST; PO, ledger, and bank statement all show the same INR 246,000 total, with PO/ledger/bank not breaking out tax separately, which is consistent with typical extraction behavior rather than an inconsistency). Dates follow a logical sequence: PO (08-01) precedes invoice (08-09), which precedes goods receipt (08-11), which precedes ledger and bank entries (08-14). Note that REC-1014 is a goods receipt, not a payment receipt, so it establishes delivery but does not itself confirm any payment-terms condition beyond delivery confirmation - however, no payment-terms document requiring a separate payment receipt is indicated as missing here since a bank statement already documents the payment. No document type expected for this transaction pattern is absent, and no vendor-specific PO-exemption pattern is relevant since a PO is present. Overall the transaction is well-supported by a complete and internally consistent document set.
